PLAY · SOUND MANIPULATION

Unicorn Sound Swap

Say the word, make the swap sound, then write the letter that changes the word into the new one.

HOW TO DO IT

Read, then draw.

Say the word, make the swap sound, then write the letter that changes the word into the new one.

A magic swap!

YOUR PENCIL CASE

Pick your tools.

Pencil, nine crayons, an eraser, undo, redo and clear appear right here and work straight on the picture. Save keeps your finished work as a picture.

MY PROGRESS

Save it to keep it.

This adventure is cleared for you the moment you save your finished picture. Nothing counts until then — opening the page is just opening the door.

Cleared! Every spell cast! Your saved work is in your downloads, and the ribbon is on in the library.

PREFER PAPER?

Print the twin.

The same picture lives in the worksheet library with its own print buttons: /worksheets/phonics/unicorn-sound-swap/. Crayons beat styluses sometimes.

FOR GROWN-UPS

Why this adventure helps.

This activity trains sound manipulation right on the adventure picture, with one short written instruction a grown-up can read aloud. Nothing is graded and nothing is scored — the win is a child who picked up a pencil, played with the sounds they hear in words, and saved work they are proud of. Saying the sounds cleanly (sss, not “suh”) as they draw is exactly how reading research says to teach them.

Prefer paper? The Unicorn Sound Swap worksheet brings the same activity to the kitchen table with a parent-read sound script and an answer line — printing a worksheet never marks a class complete.
